clue.text: Doc drinks alcohol, unknown to another dwarf

indicators.note: someone who drinks takes liquid inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a doctor is a GP, a general practitioner
a spirit, swallowed by the doctor
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Doc, one of the seven dwarfs, secretly hits the bottle and hides it from a fellow dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Doc is itself one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, so the surface invites you to stay in the cottage; the answer is another of them, and Doc becomes a GP.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy is the name of another of the seven dwarfs in the Disney Snow White film, alongside Doc.

clue.text: Shimmer from mist mostly lost in valley

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, so one of its letters goes
something lost in a place disappears inside it, so these letters sit within another word

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
mist without its first letter, keeping three of four

explanation.surface: Light gleams off mist that has mostly vanished in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' usually cuts the last letter; here it is the M of mist that goes, leaving three letters to put inside the Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine with a sparkling, wet-looking light, a near synonym of to shimmer.

clue.text: Posh little girl holds up pole to take washing off line

indicators.note: in a down entry, a thing that holds something up sits beneath it, which fixes the order of the pieces

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
the North Pole, abbreviated N
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A well-to-do small girl props up the clothes pole so the laundry can come down.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg sits below the pole in the grid, so she holds it up; the posh U comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg is to remove the clothes pegs, so taking dry laundry down from a washing line.

clue.text: Black and white plaid dress has to be taken up

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking something up means reading it from bottom to top
one part has, or holds, the other inside it
to dress something is to arrange or set it in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word plaid rearranged
taken as written apart from the infinitive marker

explanation.surface: A black-and-white tartan dress needs its hem raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken up' sounds like dressmaking; here it turns BE upwards before it goes into the rearranged plaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Piebald describes an animal, typically a horse, with irregular patches of black and white.

clue.text: Shriek after awful scare on motorway

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are mangled into a new order
one part goes on, or next to, the other, placing it after

parts.note: the word scare rearranged
M is the label of British motorways, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks after a terrible fright on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry, the same thing as a shriek, and both work as nouns here.

clue.text: Unflinchingly conservative friend's keeping money

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ally is a friend; the 's stands for 'is'
M is the economist's symbol for money supply

explanation.surface: A steady Tory pal who doesn't flinch while holding on to the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The ally keeps the M of money between its L's.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something calmly is to do it without visible fear or agitation, which is acting unflinchingly.

clue.text: Assigned by listener to approach feature editor

indicators.note: each piece approaches the next, coming up close behind it in order

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a distinguishing mark is a feature
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A job handed out by a radio listener who goes up to a newspaper's features editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature editor' reads as one job title, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or resources earmarked for a purpose are set aside or allocated to it, so assigned.

clue.text: Spotted model trained to enter races

indicators.note: something trained has been worked and shaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A spotted catwalk model has been coached to take part in races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT goes in among the rearranged letters of model, landing in the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Mottled means marked with spots or blotches of colour, so spotted in its adjectival sense.

clue.text: No letter is completely without interest

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: with no character, a character being a letter or symbol
second meaning: dull, lacking any distinctive quality

explanation.surface: Someone complains that receiving no letter at all is utterly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is jokey: a character is a printed letter, and being without one makes you literally lacking characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characterless has no distinctive traits, so it is dull; read literally, it lacks a typed character, a letter.

clue.text: First sign of spot in cheek causes speech impediment

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: lip means cheek in the sense of impudence

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of spot

explanation.surface: A pimple appearing on the cheek makes someone talk funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A lisp is a defect of speech in which s sounds are pronounced as th, a classic speech impediment.

clue.text: Thrill when English team, including Hammond initially, takes 3rd and then 2nd in rally at speed …

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a team including someone holds that person inside it

parts.note: a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
the third and then the second letter are picked from the word that follows, in that order

parts.note: the opening letter of Hammond
the third letter then the second letter of rally
a rate is a speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: An English driving team, with Richard Hammond, thrills by finishing third then second in a fast rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hammond presented the BBC car show Top Gear, which links this clue to the next one via the ellipsis; the H goes inside the team XI.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate someone is to fill them with excitement and high spirits, which is to thrill them; both are verbs.

clue.text: … shame "Top Gear" driver May doesn't finish

indicators.note: someone who doesn't finish stops short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: The Stig is the anonymous masked racing driver on the BBC car show Top Gear
May without its final letter; James May was a Top Gear presenter

explanation.surface: It is a disgrace that the Top Gear presenter James May fails to finish the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue's rally; 'Top Gear driver May' reads as one person, but it splits into the Stig and May.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone, so a shame in the sense of a social stain.

clue.text: Sure about subject

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
liable means subject to, as in liable to tax

explanation.surface: Someone is certain about the topic under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A reliable thing is dependable, a sure bet; both adjectives describe something that can be counted on.

clue.text: Present bought with crazy reduction

indicators.note: something crazy is out of its right mind, so these letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A gift picked up thanks to a wild price cut in the sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift noun but the answer is a verb, as in presenting one person to another.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce someone is to present them formally to another person, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Speak on behalf of soldier getting donation

parts.note: the RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
a present is a gift or donation

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up for a soldier who receives a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to act or speak for them, as an MP does for constituents.

clue.text: Slide for small child

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
kid is informal for a child

explanation.surface: A playground slide meant for little children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slide' suggests playground equipment, but it is the verb, as a car slides on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is an uncontrolled sliding movement, as of a vehicle on a slippery road.

clue.text: Samples prunes without number

indicators.note: without signals going without something, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to prune is to snip or trim
N is the standard abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone tastes the dried prunes, skipping one item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prunes' looks like the dried fruit; it is the verb for trimming plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip something is to taste it in small amounts, so samples, as with a wine.

clue.text: Standing sculpture captivates king

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted figure
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A standing sculpture of a figure enchants the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' looks like it describes the sculpture, but it is the noun meaning reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means standing or reputation gained through ability or achievement, as well as height.

clue.text: Guard takes worker prisoner

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second along, with it following straight after

parts.note: to guard is to defend
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A security guard seizes an employee and holds them prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes prisoner' reads as one phrase, but prisoner is the definition, the person in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant is the accused in a criminal trial, the prisoner at the bar in older courtroom language.

clue.text: Measure power and put into effect

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
force is power or strength

explanation.surface: Authorities assess their strength and then bring in a law.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting width, half an em, a convention crossword solvers learn early.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a law or rule is to compel observance of it, so to make it take effect.

clue.text: Designed navy tie with greenness in mind

indicators.note: something designed has been put together in a fresh pattern, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A navy tie was designed with environmentalism in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenness' points at eco-friendly design, but here it means inexperience.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is lack of experience or worldliness, and being green means being inexperienced.

clue.text: Insect chasing us is harmful

indicators.note: one thing chasing another comes behind it, fixing the order

parts.note: we is the subject form of us
evil means harmful or wicked

explanation.surface: A dangerous insect is pursuing us.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout, a pest of grain and stored food.

clue.text: Good wishes on parting were spoilt in fall-out

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, enclosed by it
spoilt means damaged, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the word were rearranged
fall from fall-out, with out read as outside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Fond goodbyes were ruined by a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall-out' reads as a row; split, it gives fall with out telling you it goes outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is an expression of good wishes said when people part, a goodbye.

clue.text: Partially fireproof, a brick-like material

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run spans the end of fireproof, the a and the start of brick-like

explanation.surface: A cloth that is partly flame-resistant and as tough as brick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is woven or knitted cloth, a textile material for clothes or furnishings.

clue.text: Brownish insect eats figs endlessly

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: with no ends means both first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: figs with both its ends gone

explanation.surface: A brownish bug feeds on figs without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it means nonstop eating; it trims both ends of figs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale sandy fawn colour, a light shade of brown.

clue.text: Foreman with XL mask?

parts.note: XL, extra large, is a super size
a visor is a face shield or mask

explanation.surface: A big foreman wearing an extra-large face mask.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose link between XL and super.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees workers, which is exactly a foreman's role on a factory floor or building site.

clue.text: Aim for 1,000 to leave store with 500 entering

indicators.note: one letter leaves while another comes in to take its place
the replacement letter enters where the departed one stood

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish furniture store
K stands for a thousand, as in a 50K salary
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone sets a target of a thousand leaving the shop, with five hundred coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the store is swapped for the D.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be an aim or intention, as in 'the idea is to finish by noon'.

clue.text: Former lover's out lots and celebrates!

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ex is a former partner; the 's stands for 'is'
the word lots rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is out on the town a great deal, partying.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol something is to praise it enthusiastically, which is to celebrate it in words.

clue.text: Year at sea follows first half of rest cure

indicators.note: what follows comes after, placing the sea and year behind the other piece
keep only the opening half of the word that comes next

parts.note: the front two of its four letters
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A year at sea after a little rest is the best cure.
explanation.walkthrough: Year at sea attaches the Y to the Med, and that whole piece follows the half-rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a medicine or treatment that relieves illness, so a cure.
